items.note: Cooperative creamery association organized by Larrow Valley farmers 1889, main creamery Larrow Green 1891, Gideon Vose as founder (Story 1/4). Core fact present.
Article VII given as payment by butterfat test not milk weight, but the second bolded element 'the test of the station where he delivers governs' is absent from Section A.
Section A never says payment by test is what made a wrong test cost money (only in B3, which cannot credit A).
Only Hobart Sill named as buttermaker; Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent from Section A.
Selby Vose, son of Gideon, manager (Story 4); nephew rejected. Year 1913 not in A (B3 gives 1911, deducted separately).
Station-gain ledger line not described in Section A.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896 (Story 1). Borrowed Larrow Green glass not mentioned; core fact present.
Weighing / composite sample / percent-on-neck mechanism not described.
Outfit bought from Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897.
6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Story 2: the 0.19 shortfall ran uniformly in every month, June flush and February alike.
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, none in the county.
Keddie tester from opening for 29 seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book routine/columns/crossed corrections not described; A instead garbles him as receiving a weigh book from Brant.
Summary leaf with 1896 = 3.80 and 3.61 from 1898 not given; both figures required.
Glass broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure nine weeks to 10 July, tests higher then fell back, question mark (Story 3). 3.80 figure absent but core fact present.
Married to Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; Emmet the largest holder/hauler.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why is absent (both bolded).
Died 1934 with imputation still on him.
Hessel Bottom's six farms; Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book garbled: 'Ansel received his weigh book from Emmet Brant... noting when the station's scale agreed with his own'. No 1 Jan 1897, attribution wrong.
States Hollow-vs-Green as 3.61 vs 3.78 = 'a deficiency of 0.19' — the gap conflation the key says loses the item.
Grigg committee 'sampled herds across 1908' (whole-year corruption F096) instead of Jan-Mar 1908.
Brant's 1910 200,000 lb at 3.42 and proportional loss not in Section A.
Weigh book's passage to Roy Brant 1929 and loan to Ivy 1958 not in Section A.
Only 'the cheese factory over the ridge'; no Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, or Jerome Cudd.
Four of the six farms hauled over the ridge in summer, Ostrey Hollow rest of year. 1915 missing; core fact present.
Independence of the Alder Corners test not stated.
0.19 higher at Alder Corners over sixteen seasons not stated.
Same milk tested differently in two buildings not stated.
Rosalie Cudd not mentioned.
Strawn's lactometer visits 'from 1908 forward' (NT-23) instead of circuit 1907-1936.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
June 1923, pipettes run against a burette, whole lot condemned.
No statement that Strawn wrote no figure / made no report beyond the condemnation.
1924 average given as 3.85 (corruption), not 3.80.
Crate to loft present, but 1947 transfer of notebooks to college library absent (both bolded).
Petition January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May, two sittings in weigh room.
Three theories argued, cause not established. Misattributes theft to Vose, but attributions are unbolded context.
Four books incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody laid them side by side.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; award $3,800 without admission.
Award as one fifth of $19,000 charged to the station-gain account not stated.
Granddaughter, grad student at State Agricultural College, Farland, with Leland Vaught.
Not framed as Ivy assembling records never before in one room.
February 1958, crate in station loft, nine survived.
Mean given as 16.27 c.c., short 1.33 (7.6%) — NT-1 corruption.
Says tests short by 7.6%, not 95% of true / 3.61 vs 3.80.
Gives 19,600 and 67,000 lb as competing figures; no 40M/76,000/$19,000/ledger identity.
Bulletin 471 Oct 1958 and '24 years after his death' present, but the 35- and 33-year intervals (same bolded element) absent; Story 6 gives wrong intervals.
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan, Ansel's son, Ivy his daughter.
Second cousins, children of first cousins Roy and Duncan.
Abstention A08: full vs half siblings never raised.
Gideon Vose; nephew rejected.
Gideon established the payment-by-test system that made the low tests damaging.
Abstention A01: never says the sources cannot settle it; treats Duncan's denial as contradicting the talk.
Presents a family member's denial as 'direct knowledge' disposing of the claim, contrary to what is established.
True average 3.91, shortfall 0.30.
Answers 67,000 lb.
400 lb (3.62 true test).
72 pipettes correct but shortfall 1.33 c.c.; both required.
26 years 1 month; 21 full years 1902-1923.
Abstention A02: asserts 1,100,000 lb.
Variable: the station's measuring glass.
Herds, pasture, season, tester, machinery held constant.
Higher through nine weeks, fell back on 10 July; 3.80 and 3.61 stated in C1.
Equipment not herds/milk/men; limit: does not establish magnitude.
1911 interval, Strawn lactometer, cream arriving heavy (Sill) from r22/r24/r16/r14.
Independence argued; 1911 interval survives without 1958 measurement.
Abstention A09: asserts Teague never questioned the entries.
Yes, citing 1902 grievance and 1919 circular.
Only ledger signing and 1919 circular; gives manager from 1911 and says he argued theft at hearing.
Abstention A03: verdict 'His knowledge was of effect, not cause' / 'knew something was systematically wrong'.
Nine vs six weeks (by dates), $3,800 vs $3,500 (majority of sources), $77.93 vs $77.39 (invoice sum), son vs nephew (Kyle). Station-opening and butterfat-total resolutions are wrong.
Explicitly states no two narrators carry the same wrong value.
A04, A06, A10 not treated as unsettleable; A04 asserted as accident.
Says no self-contradictions found.
Cause from 16.27 c.c./7.6%, 1924 at 3.85; no 0.95 / 5% of 3.80 derivation.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer.
Theft defeated by cream arriving heavy and 1911 interval.
Uses Bulletin 214 'two tenths in winter' (corruption) rather than five hundredths; no Alder Corners or three-month defeater.
Abstention A07: 'The board did not examine the glassware.'
Abstention A05: 'Ansel Keddie believed the problem was in the glass.'
Body is about 165 words (plus title); run claims 147.
At most one or two record series named (1958 measurement).
Contains 16.27 c.c.
1897, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named; both ends covered.
